summary: Candidate refactors the upstream read-grant consistency assertions in CHECK_MASTER_GRANTS. The original per-bit loop and separate srgrant check are replaced by an equivalent assert on srgrant == (rgrant != 0), a one-hot match rgrant == (1 << srindex), a range check srindex <= NS, and conditional reciprocal slave-side checks for srindex < NS. The error-route exclusivity is unchanged. I find the same obligation, not a weakened or different one, assuming standard Verilog width semantics for the shift. Frontend PASS is only elaboration; no formal proof is claimed.

changes.title: Read-grant consistency assertions refactored
changes.analysis: Upstream lines 1743-1754, inside CHECK_MASTER_GRANTS, iterate iM=0..NS and, when rgrant[N][iM] is set, assert (rgrant[N] ^ (1<<iM))==0, srgrant[N], srindex[N]==iM, and for iM<NS assert mrgrant[iM] and mrindex[iM]==N. Upstream also has separate blocks asserting srgrant[N] -> rgrant[N]!=0 and rrequest[N][NS] -> rrequest[N][NS-1:0]==0. Candidate replaces this with one always block: assert(srgrant[N] == (rgrant[N] != 0)); if srgrant, assert(srindex[N] <= NS); assert(rgrant[N] == ({{(NS){1'b0}}, 1'b1} << srindex[N])); if srindex<NS, assert mrgrant[srindex] and mrindex[srindex]==N; and the same rrequest error-route exclusivity. The equivalence assertion covers both original srgrant directions. The one-hot equality covers the original per-bit XOR and srindex match. The conditional reciprocal check matches the original iM<NS branch. For NS=8, the shift literal has NS+1=9 bits, so the one-hot expression is correctly sized. No new assumptions or fixed outputs are introduced in candidate/axilxbar.v; candidate/environment.md states no harness changes. Concrete sequences that both versions should flag: srgrant=1,rgrant=0; rgrant=2'b11,srgrant=1; rgrant=1<<2,srgrant=1,srindex=3; rgrant=1<<(NS-1),srgrant=1,srindex=NS-1,mrgrant[NS-1]=0.
changes.property_impact: Same obligation. The candidate is a refactor of the same read-grant consistency property: granted read => one selected route at srindex, with reciprocal slave-side grant/index for real slaves. It is not narrower and does not appear to introduce a different obligation. No property weakening identified.
changes.concern: No formal proof run is provided; frontend PASS only shows elaboration. The candidate was not shown to prove or fail the upstream assertions. The proof target parameter differs from upstream SBY (C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH=32 vs 16), so upstream proof status is not inherited.

open_questions: Does the candidate pass the same formal proof under the specified parameter variant? No formal result is supplied.
Are there any other candidate differences outside the read-grant block? Only axilxbar.v and environment.md were inspected here; candidate/frontend.txt only reports elaboration.

Could the shift-width or assert-order in the candidate cause tool-specific differences? Standard Verilog gives an NS+1-bit left operand and srindex<=NS guard, so no semantic gap was identified, but a formal run would confirm.
